unresolved_core_findings.title: Company-defense outcome remains unresolved when an active alliance exceeds attack strength
unresolved_core_findings.finding: A standard Events in India defense can have attack strength1 and only one active, bought strength2 alliance available. The summary reproduces the printed equality test and explicitly declines to decide this case. The supplied rules do not explicitly say whether excess alliance strength may be wasted/capped, whether full exhaustion succeeds, or whether literal non-equality forces Region Loss. This leaves an in-scope core outcome without a complete adjudication.

source_refs.evidence: Alliance strength is available for defense; each piece is usable once and strength cannot be split among more than one purpose.
The printed instruction requires equal strength or as many pieces as possible, and says a non-equal result causes Crisis success/Region Loss.

source_refs.file: supplements/pnp/Rulebooks/John Company Player Aid (Front and Back).pdf
source_refs.section: Crisis table, Attack on the Company row and result header
source_refs.evidence: Defender strength is exhausted Regiments, Officers and Local Alliances; result header says defender wins ties. This supports a comparative-defense reading but gives no concrete excess-alliance example or explicit cap/discard rule.

unresolved_core_findings.independent_source_assessment: Literal p33 non-equality wording could be read to make an exhausted strength2 alliance fail against attack1. Alternatively, p22 use-for-one-purpose language and the official aid’s strength-comparison table support wasting excess on a single defense. Neither is asserted here as a definitive designer ruling. The aid is relevant contrary/contextual evidence, so the question cannot honestly be closed merely by assuming greater-or-equal defense or merely by quoting p33 equality without addressing alliance counting.
unresolved_core_findings.impact: The unresolved branch determines unrest clearance/trophies versus Region Loss, officer rout and Company Standing loss, potentially ending the game; it is core multiplayer procedure and not an excluded optional mode.
unresolved_core_findings.repair_advice: Obtain a publisher/designer clarification of this concrete case: Company region faces attack strength1; only active Army resource is a bought strength2 alliance. Must it be exhausted, does it defend successfully, and is any excess strength discarded while the whole piece becomes unavailable? Cite that ruling, encode the procedure and re-audit. Until then retain the explicit source-gap disclosure and unverified status; do not award complete core signoff.
